questions.q: What does the Filter transformation remove from the raw sales data, and why is it applied first?
options: Cancelled and test orders, applied first so downstream steps process less data and totals aren't inflated
Orders from a specific region, applied last to keep totals accurate
Nothing — filtering happens automatically without a dedicated transformation
Duplicate rows only, applied after the aggregate
questions.explain: Filtering first removes cancelled orders and internal test transactions before any join or aggregate, so a cancelled order can never inflate a regional total downstream.

questions.q: Why must the join transformations happen before the aggregate?
options: You can't group by Region if the row doesn't have a Region column yet
Joins and aggregates can happen in any order with no difference
The aggregate transformation automatically performs joins internally
It's arbitrary — either order produces identical results
questions.explain: Since Region and Category come from separate dimension tables, they must be joined into the row before the Aggregate transformation can group by them.

questions.q: Why is OrderCount added to the aggregate alongside TotalSales, even though it wasn't explicitly requested?
options: It gives useful context — a large total from few orders tells a different story than the same total from many
It's required by the Aggregate transformation and can't be omitted
It replaces TotalSales entirely
It has no real purpose and was added arbitrarily
questions.explain: OrderCount is nearly free to compute alongside the sum and gives the 8 AM meeting meaningful context that a raw dollar total alone wouldn't provide.

questions.q: Why is the sink's Update method set to Overwrite rather than Insert?
options: So every morning's run replaces yesterday's totals cleanly instead of accumulating duplicates if run twice
Overwrite is the only update method Azure SQL Database sinks support
Insert mode is faster, so Overwrite is used only for testing
Update method has no effect on how data lands in the sink
questions.explain: Overwrite ensures the curated table always reflects a single clean set of totals for the day, rather than risking duplicate rows if the pipeline runs more than once.

questions.q: Why isn't a green "Succeeded" pipeline status sufficient proof that the transformation is correct?
options: A successful run only confirms the pipeline executed — it doesn't verify the actual computed numbers are accurate
Succeeded status is always a guarantee of correct data, no further check needed
Pipeline status and data correctness are the same thing
There's no way to verify data correctness in Data Factory at all
questions.explain: Verifying correctness requires actually checking the numbers — like comparing a region's total against a manual query — since a successful run status says nothing about whether the transformation logic produced the right values.
